blindSummary:
No trans-specific incident series was found for this state/province, but the dossier documents 138 recorded acts of torture or other ill-treatment in detention committed by police and military in the highland interior and its surrounding regencies between September 2021 and Q1 2025, "with almost no consequences"; most victims were young men, several minors, arrested chiefly for alleged links to armed groups or protest participation. Named arbitrary-detention cases include three local men detained by officers at a regional airport in the highland interior on 26 July 2025 as two of them were preparing to depart for the main city to continue their studies. Q3 2025 saw a notable increase in military deployments and operations in the highlands, causing further internal displacement. For any visitor, including a transgender one, the probability that police contact escalates into unlawful detention and ill-treatment is documented. This is an amplifier finding on non-trans-specific evidence, not an independent conclusion about trans people.

Elsewhere in the country an enacted bylaw with specified administrative penalties creates one kind of exposure; here the documented torture-and-arrest pattern raises the severity of any encounter with security forces, without a trans-specific legal basis being needed.
blindSourceSummaries: Torture-monitoring briefing (July 2025): police and military in this state/province and the surrounding highlands committed 138 recorded acts of torture or ill-treatment in detention (Sept 2021-Q1 2025) with almost no consequences; victims mostly males under 24 plus 7 women and 7 minors; arrests largely for alleged armed-group links or demonstrations; deaths during torture documented in operation areas; incidents catalogued on a local detention-monitoring database.

Human-rights monitor case file: police arbitrarily detained three local men at a regional airport in the highland interior on 26 July 2025 - two were preparing to fly to the main city to continue their studies, one an airport employee accompanying them; an example of airport-stop arbitrary detention any traveller can be swept into.

Human-rights monitor quarterly report Q3 2025: notable increase in military deployments and operations in the highland regions since August 2025, further internal displacement, fatal shootings and arbitrary detentions, and failure of accountability mechanisms.
blindTangential: The new national penal code (Jan 2026) applies fully here; the unit-specific factor is not an anti-LGBT bylaw (none found) but a documented security-force abuse pattern that worsens any police contact, including for gender-nonconforming travellers.
